blocks.label: Voice description
blocks.body: English, Received Pronunciation (not General American). British woman, late 30s, dry and unhurried. Documentary narrator. Wry, authoritative. Husky in texture, with an even, unhurried delivery and clean articulation. Broadcast quality recording.

blocks.label: Preview text: must agree with the description
blocks.body: There is a moment, right before the bell, when the noise drops away. You can hear the ropes settle, and your own breathing, and nothing else at all. That is the moment the whole thing turns on

blocks.label: Do not include
blocks.body: No reverb, echo, delay or any other acoustic or effects language. Voice Design models the voice, not the room.

flat: English, Received Pronunciation (not General American). British woman, late 30s, dry and unhurried. Documentary narrator. Wry, authoritative. Husky in texture, with an even, unhurried delivery and clean articulation. Broadcast quality recording.
notes: Use BCP-47 tags with the dialect, not just the language: en-AU, es-MX, pt-BR. The dialect is where the quality is.
Speaker similarity runs 0 to 10 and defaults to 7. Raise it when the original performance is the point.
warnings: API limit is 3GB per file, 180 minutes in-app. Dubbing Studio (v1) is the editable-transcript path and caps much lower at 45 minutes.
Concurrency is three jobs on self-serve. Plan batches around it.

variations.name: Half a step slower
variations.text: Drop speed to 0.92 and raise stability by 0.1. Read for an audience of one, not a room.

variations.name: Warmer, less formal
variations.text: Rewrite the script in contractions, add one ellipsis before the last clause, and lower stability to widen the range.

variations.name: Cold read
variations.text: Strip every tag and let punctuation alone carry the prosody. Useful as a control to hear what the tags are really doing.
